measurement: Lighthouse 13.5.0 lab tests; homepage only. No CrUX real-user data was available. Scores and timings vary between runs.
changes: Self-hosted the same Inter and Fraunces fonts with original licenses; removed the shared Google font import and redundant matching font links. Custom font configurations were preserved.
Preloaded homepage fonts; deferred the below-fold homepage process stylesheet with a no-JavaScript fallback.
Created responsive team-photo sizes while retaining the original image.
Reused a lossless WebP logo with reserved dimensions in the homepage and shared desktop/mobile navigation; lazy-loaded the footer logo.
Loaded slideshow images progressively rather than downloading all hidden slides at startup; held the current image until the next image decoded.
Paused slideshow animation off-screen, in background tabs, and for reduced-motion preferences.
Fixed homepage trust-label horizontal overflow at 320-pixel viewport width.

verification.notes: 320px tested on homepage; 390px and 1280px tested on representative pages. No horizontal overflow or broken loaded images were observed. Homepage mobile menu and empty required-field validation passed without submitting a lead. Critical desktop homepage element dimensions matched baseline exactly; mobile heading dimensions matched baseline.
verification.staticReview: Non-homepage HTML diffs were mechanically restricted to shared font links and cache-version references. Separate client projects and unrelated untracked assets were not staged.
verification.deployment: Both code commits were pushed to origin/main; matching GitHub Pages deployments completed successfully. The published homepage was refreshed and verified to reference the new shared script and WebP logo.

remainingOpportunities: GitHub Pages controls cache lifetimes and response headers; these cannot be changed by adding server configuration files to this static repository.
Shared CSS still includes unused rules. Splitting it by route is a larger follow-up requiring wider visual regression testing.
Lighthouse still flags approximately 100 KiB of mobile image-delivery savings and render-blocking styles. Current photo quality and approved design were preserved.
Accessibility remains 91: contrast, touch-target spacing, and heading-order findings require a dedicated follow-up. A performance score is not an accessibility certification.
No whole-site PageSpeed score or real-user Core Web Vitals pass is implied. Internal pages received functional/responsive spot checks and automated content/link tests, not individual Lighthouse runs.
